note: GDPR submodule to mark entity fields as personal data with Right-to-Access (rta: inc|maybe|no) and Right-to-be-Forgotten (rtf: anonymize|remove|maybe|no) settings + an anonymizer plugin id. No settings form of its own (configure=null); GDPR settings are added to each field's edit form and a report lives at /admin/reports/fields/gdpr-fields (route gdpr_fields.fields_list, permission view gdpr fields). Per-field metadata is stored in a CONFIG ENTITY gdpr_fields_config (id = entity type; config name gdpr_fields.gdpr_fields_config.<entity_type>) under bundles[<bundle>][<field>] = {enabled, rta, rtf, anonymizer, notes, relationship, sars_filename, entity_type_id}; a simplified copy is mirrored to field third-party settings (gdpr_fields_rta/gdpr_fields_rtf). Permissions view/edit gdpr fields. Service gdpr_fields.collector + EntityTraversal walk the entity graph for gdpr_tasks. Requires gdpr + anonymizer. Medium/hard ground in the gdpr_fields_config config entity for the user 'mail' field (user bundle = 'user').

evals.prompt: In the Drupal gdpr_fields module, where is a field's GDPR configuration (whether it is personal data and how to handle it) stored, and how is it keyed?
evals.expected_output: In a config entity gdpr_fields_config (one per entity type, id = entity type, config name gdpr_fields.gdpr_fields_config.<entity_type>), under bundles[<bundle>][<field>] with keys enabled, rta, rtf, anonymizer, notes, relationship, sars_filename. A simplified copy is mirrored to the field's third-party settings.

evals.prompt: In gdpr_fields, what do the rta and rtf settings mean and what values can they take?
evals.expected_output: rta = Right to Access (values inc, maybe, no) controls whether a field is included in a Subject Access Request export; rtf = Right to be Forgotten (values anonymize, remove, maybe, no) controls whether a removal request anonymizes or deletes the field. rtf=anonymize uses the field's configured anonymizer plugin.

evals.prompt: Which permissions does gdpr_fields define and where is the report of all fields' GDPR status?
evals.expected_output: Permissions 'view gdpr fields' and 'edit gdpr fields'. The report is at /admin/reports/fields/gdpr-fields (route gdpr_fields.fields_list, requires 'view gdpr fields').

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the user 'mail' field has been configured in gdpr_fields for right-to-be-forgotten handling. Inspect the live gdpr_fields configuration and state which anonymizer plugin is set for the user mail field and its RTF setting.
evals.expected_output: In gdpr_fields_config.user, bundles.user.mail has anonymizer = email_anonymizer with rtf = anonymize (and enabled true, rta inc).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use gdpr_fields to mark the user account's email (user entity, 'mail' field) as personal data: enable it, set Right to be Forgotten to 'anonymize', and choose the email_anonymizer. Apply the change to the live site configuration.
evals.expected_output: The gdpr_fields_config entity for 'user' has bundles.user.mail with enabled=true, rtf='anonymize', anonymizer='email_anonymizer'. Do it via the field edit form's GDPR settings, or with GdprFieldConfigEntity::load('user')/create + GdprField setters (setEnabled/setRtf/setAnonymizer) + setField + save.
